question.text: If a USDINR call option at strike 83 has a premium of Rs. 0.35 and USDINR spot is 83.20, what is the time value?

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 70 of the source defines time value as premium minus intrinsic value and gives call intrinsic value as max(S - X, 0). Here S = 83.20 and X = 83, so intrinsic value = Rs. 0.20 and time value = 0.35 - 0.20 = Rs. 0.15. The Trap: Treating the full Rs. 0.35 premium as time value ignores the in-the-money intrinsic component; using 0.55 double-counts. Note: Page 70 also states that time value becomes zero at expiry, so this Rs. 0.15 will erode as the option approaches its expiry date.
